You are reviewing a code diff for EFFICIENCY issues only: wasted work, redundant computation or repeated I/O, independent operations run sequentially when they could be concurrent, blocking work added to startup/hot paths, or long-lived objects/closures that keep large scopes alive. Do not look for correctness bugs.

Context: this diff is from a session that got a real llama-completion binary running under an "andesim" hybrid RISC-V simulator (QEMU + a cycle-accurate RTL simulator called vsim), fixing ELEN=32 vector-width crashes in llama.cpp's ggml library (a CPU math library for LLM inference) and adding a `--step-timeout-ms` CLI flag to the andesim driver.

Two repos are involved:
1. `/home/nick/work/andesim` (the simulator driver, C++) — diff at `/tmp/claude-1002/-home-nick-work-andesim/5eeca9dc-9078-4a2c-9aec-f331d1142619/scratchpad/simplify_andesim.diff`
2. `/home/nick/work/llama.cpp` (the LLM inference engine, ggml's CPU backend, C) — diff at `/tmp/claude-1002/-home-nick-work-andesim/5eeca9dc-9078-4a2c-9aec-f331d1142619/scratchpad/simplify_llamacpp.diff`

Read both diff files. Note: each diff is the FULL uncommitted diff of the touched files (nothing has been committed this session), so it may include some pre-existing uncommitted work from earlier in the same effort mixed in with the new work — focus your attention on what looks like genuinely NEW logic (added functions, added CLI flags, added helpers), not on isolated pre-existing lines that happen to be nearby.

This is performance-sensitive code in two specific ways worth extra scrutiny:
1. `ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/quants.c`: `quantize_row_q8_0`/`quantize_row_q8_1` were changed from a hand-vectorized RVV implementation to calling a portable scalar `_ref` fallback, because the vectorized version used a vector width (LMUL=8 for float ops) this specific hardware target doesn't support. This function is called on a HOT PATH (once per activation row during every matmul). Read the actual diff and the full functions (use Read on `/home/nick/work/llama.cpp/ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/quants.c` around `quantize_row_q8_0`/`quantize_row_q8_1` for full context) — is there a narrower-LMUL vectorized alternative that was available but not used (e.g. could LMUL=2 or LMUL=4 have kept SOME vectorization instead of going fully scalar)? Note: this is a real design tradeoff already made deliberately for correctness+simplicity — only flag it if you see something the diff's own reasoning missed, not as a "you should have vectorized it" nag independent of the tradeoff already documented in the diff/comments.
2. `runtime/handler.c` (andesim): the new `raw_print_hex()` calls happen unconditionally at the START of every trap, before checking anything about the trap type. Is this reasonable (it's an error/crash path, not a hot path, so "efficiency" barely applies) or does it do anything wasteful even for a rare-event handler (e.g. redundant work, an unbounded loop, computing something not used)?

Also check `driver/cmd_run.cpp`'s new `--step-timeout-ms` parsing block for any wasted work (e.g. redundant string operations, unnecessary intermediate allocations) — but this runs once per CLI invocation, so weight any finding accordingly (a microsecond here doesn't matter; only flag something that's actually notable).

Report only real findings with file, line, a one-line summary, and the cheaper alternative. If you find nothing significant (likely, given this is mostly error-path/CLI-parse code, not hot-path code), say so plainly and don't manufacture findings. Keep the report under 350 words.

#ifndef ANDESIM_HTIF_CLIENT_H
#define ANDESIM_HTIF_CLIENT_H

/* HTIF syscall-window client: the uncached SimControl mailbox protocol
 * shared by every andesim runtime payload (vplat today; vlinux next). The
 * window lives in DEVICE space (PMA-uncached on every engine), so the
 * exchange is coherent by construction on any cache hierarchy, including a
 * private write-back L2 (ax66 PL2C) that a cacheable-RAM mailbox cannot
 * survive: the guest would read its own stale copy of the host's result,
 * and no guest-side CCTL sequence can fix that (the VA-scoped forms trap
 * on RVH cores, the ALL forms drop unrelated dirty lines).
 *
 *   stdio (fd 0-2)  ATCUART100 UART2: THR @0xf0300020, LSR @0xf0300034.
 *   file io (fd>2)  the SimControl syscall WINDOW @0xe0080800: eight u64
 *                   arg/result slots + a data area for payloads, doorbell
 *                   @0xe0080028. Served host-side (vsim: sim_control.hpp
 *                   dispatch_window; QEMU: andes_ae350.c's mirror).
 *
 * No semihosting, no ecall, and no "which engine am I on" probe -- hybrid
 * migrates the running process between engines, so any boot-time detection
 * would go stale at the handoff. Every call must be engine-blind.
 */

#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <sys/types.h>

/* HTIF syscall numbers -- must match the table in the vsim repo's
 * src/platform/sim_control.hpp (and the QEMU mirror device). */
#define VH_SYS_GETTIMEOFDAY 5
#define VH_SYS_OPEN         6
#define VH_SYS_WRITE        7
#define VH_SYS_GETCWD       8
#define VH_SYS_LSEEK        9
#define VH_SYS_READ         10
#define VH_SYS_FLEN         11
#define VH_SYS_CLOSE        12
#define VH_SYS_ACCESS       13
#define VH_SYS_FACCESSAT    14
#define VH_SYS_FSTAT        15
#define VH_SYS_FSTATAT      16
#define VH_SYS_LINK         17
#define VH_SYS_LSTAT        18
#define VH_SYS_STAT         19
#define VH_SYS_OPENAT       20
#define VH_SYS_RENAME       21
#define VH_SYS_UNLINK       22

/* Window layout -- must match the hosts (vsim src/platform/sim_control.hpp
 * SYSCALL_WINDOW_*; QEMU hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c ANDESIM_SYSCALL_*). All
 * guest accesses are u64 loads/stores (the access width every engine
 * already proves out on the legacy 0x10 doorbell). */
#define WIN_DATA_VA 0xe0080840UL
#define WIN_DATA_SIZE (0x800u - 0x40u) /* 1984 bytes, 8-aligned */

/* Console output; blocks until UART2's transmit-holding register drains. */
void htif_uart_putc(char c);

/* One window syscall: stage the slots, ring the doorbell, read the result.
 * The doorbell write is an uncached device store, so the host has served
 * the call before the store retires; the fence orders the result load. */
intptr_t htif_syscall(uint64_t n, uint64_t a0, uint64_t a1, uint64_t a2,
                       uint64_t a3);

/* Raw copies into/out of the window data area (u64 accesses only). `woff`
 * is a byte offset into the data area and must be 8-aligned. */
void htif_win_store(size_t woff, const void* src, size_t len);
void htif_win_load(void* dst, size_t woff, size_t len);

/* Stage a string at data-area offset `woff`; returns the byte offset just
 * past its NUL, rounded up to 8, or (size_t)-1 if it does not fit. */
size_t htif_win_store_str(size_t woff, const char* s);

/* Marshaling helpers for the recurring one/two-string-argument shapes. */
intptr_t htif_call_str(uint64_t n, const char* s, uint64_t a1, uint64_t a2);
intptr_t htif_call_str2(uint64_t n, const char* s0, const char* s1);

/* fd>2 write/read, chunked through the window data area (WIN_DATA_SIZE
 * bytes per round trip); stops early on a short transfer, same contract as
 * a POSIX write()/read(). Callers own the fd<=2 (console) special case. */
ssize_t htif_write(int fd, const void* ptr, size_t len);
ssize_t htif_read(int fd, void* buf, size_t len);

/* Positional read: seeks to `offset`, reads `len` bytes via htif_read,
 * then restores the fd's original position -- there is no pread window
 * op, only lseek+read, so this is the only way to honor pread(2)'s "does
 * not disturb the fd's current offset" contract on top of them. Shared by
 * every positional-read caller (syscall pread64, file-backed mmap) so the
 * save/restore sequence exists in exactly one place. */
ssize_t htif_pread(int fd, void* buf, size_t len, long offset);

#endif /* ANDESIM_HTIF_CLIENT_H */
